Direct parent-child process creation in kernel memory telemetry. reader_sl.exe records InheritedFromUniqueProcessId (PPID) == 1484 (explorer.exe) with matching CreateTime, confirmed by windows.pstree hierarchy.
Windows Session Manager subsystem process (smss.exe) spawned the logon executive (winlogon.exe). Validated by kernel PPID binding and temporal sequence (delta +1.0s).

Cridex banking trojan process hollowed / injected malicious code into reader_sl.exe. Volatility malfind identified PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE unbacked VAD allocation at 0x3D0000 with executable payload assembly header.
Reversed parent-child assertion. reader_sl.exe is the spawned child, not the parent of explorer.exe.
Print Spooler service and Windows Update client spawned by separate parent services with 70s delta. Shared SYSTEM user account is incidental system context without causal connection.

Both explorer.exe and reader_sl.exe contain PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE unbacked VAD allocations indicative of Cridex. However, memory dump telemetry lacks handle tracing or cross-process thread injection records to confirm whether explorer injected reader_sl or if both were injected by an earlier uncaptured process.
